messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Service error rate spike detected on inference-rope pool (ntk-yaRN). 5xx rate > 4% for 3m. Auto-pager triggered.

sam: oncall here, looking now. which clusters?

incident-bot: Affected: rope-ntk-us-east-1a, rope-yarn-us-east-1b. Symptoms: KV cache growth + continuous-batching latency climb.

tara: saw similar pattern earlier this month — sliding-window prefetch combined with longctx growth caused kv_key cardinality to explode. could be same root.

anjali: confirmed logs: heavy prefetch churn, lots of small KV inserts then immediate evictions. example log snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T21:12:03Z] kv.cache.insert key=len-20480:id=0x8f... size=12kb
[2026-03-15T21:12:03Z] kv.cache.evict key=len-128:id=0x8f... reason=thrash
[2026-03-15T21:12:04Z] continuous.batch.enqueue size=256 seq=987654
```

matt: customer impact? any timeouts/401s?

anjali: 502s increasing for a subset of active customers—mostly long-context experimental workloads (ntk > 32k). Error rate highest for a small set of heavy routings.

jess: marking Sev2 for now. paging the infra team. cc @matt for customer comms. :pager:

sam: quick mitigation plan: 1) temporarily cap continuous-batch max_size=64 2) reduce sliding_window_prefetch:window_ms from 3000 -> 300 3) force kv eviction sweep on affected pools 4) rollback longctx prefetch feature flags to safe mode. I'll run 1-3 now.

matt: agree. I'll prepare an outbound to affected customers after we have metrics. keep short note: degraded latency, occasional 5xx, mitigation in progress.

sam: running command to set batch cap: ```
curl -XPOST https://control-plane/api/v1/pools/rope-ntk-us-east-1a/config \
  -d '{"continuous_batch.max_size":64}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```
deploy-bot: Config change queued for rope-ntk-us-east-1a by sam. Plan: gradual apply across nodes (1m stagger).

sam: reducing prefetch window on yarn pool too: ```
PATCH /pools/rope-yarn-us-east-1b/config HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
{ "sliding_window.prefetch_ms": 300 }
```

anjali: forced eviction sweep started with admin tool: `kvctl sweep --pool rope-ntk-us-east-1a --mode aggressive`

incident-bot: Noted: config changes applied to first wave. Monitor dashboards for 5xx and kv.size metrics.

sam: immediate telemetry: kv.key_count dropping, batch latency median down ~30%, 5xx rate falling but still elevated (1.1%).

tara: good. next: disable longctx prefetch flag (feature.longctx_prefetch=false) for canary customers only, until we root-cause.

matt: drafted customer note: "We're seeing intermittent errors for long-context requests and are mitigating. No data exposure. We'll follow up with timeline after stabilization." wait for final numbers before send.

jess: people on rotation: sam -> tara (handoff in 20m) -> anjali. add postmortem owners.

sam: handing off to tara. I pushed the runbook steps, monitoring links, and the admin commands I ran to the incident doc. Tara, you're lead.

tara: taking over. thanks. first tasks: watch for regrowth over next 30m, patch the runtime to clamp KV key namespace generation (avoid len-based keys when ntk>8k). scheduling hotfix if we see any resurgence.

anjali: note: metric 'kv.kv_namespace.cardinality' peaked at 4.2M keys on yarn pool. prefetch combinatorics + per-request longctx tokens caused namespace explosion. adding to postmortem.

matt: customers notified (initial). I'll update with ETA for full resolution (depends on hotfix test).

tara: if regrowth observed, immediate next action: toggle continuous_batch.enabled=false for affected pools (will spike tail latency but stops inflight growth). prefer that over customer errors.

sam: reaction from one SRE: (reacted with :eyes:)

incident-bot: Auto-escalation threshold cleared (5xx < 1.5%). Incident status: Stabilizing.

tara: still watching. scheduling hotfix deploy in 45m to clamp key naming + reduce prefetch scope. Postmortem owners: anjali (root cause), sam (mitigations timeline), matt (customer comms).

matt: assigning follow-up: add regression tests around sliding-window + longctx interactions (fail if kv.key_count > 100k in synthetic run).

jess: thanks team. tagging for postmortem: sev2->assign->72h SLA for writeup.

tara: final note before I step out: avoid full rollback; prefer targeted runtime clamps. will update on status in #incidents thread.

sam: handing off ack. staying available for questions.

incident-bot: Thread closed for immediate paging; ongoing updates in thread."
